ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Query-to-Gaussian rendering as self-supervised pretraining for sparse detectors
PROPOSAL: Pre-train a Sparse4D detector on unlabeled six-camera clips from nuScenes by letting each instance query emit a handful of 3D Gaussians. Splat those Gaussians into the current and neighbouring frames using relative ego poses, and train with photometric and rendered-depth consistency only. Use a ResNet-50 backbone, 24 epochs, and 704x256 inputs. Then fine-tune on 10% of the labeled scenes with the standard detection loss, and transfer the same query embeddings and decoder weights to a StreamPETR detector. Report mean average precision and nuScenes detection score on the validation split.
CONTROLS: Compare against random initialisation and against an ImageNet-only backbone with the identical fine-tuning schedule. Compare against dense rendering pretraining (UniPAD-style) that transfers through the backbone alone. Repeat each run with three seeds and vary the labeled fraction over 5%, 10% and 25%.
COST: 160
PREDICTION: We expect a gain of two to three mean average precision points at 10% labels that shrinks as more labels are added. The idea fails if ImageNet-only initialisation matches the pretrained model within seed variation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Temporal depth consistency pretraining for sparse occupancy queries
PROPOSAL: Train a SparseOcc-style occupancy decoder on unlabeled multi-view sequences from Occ3D scenes without any voxel labels. Each query predicts a semantic Gaussian and a depth, and a differentiable rasteriser projects it into the camera of the next frame, where the loss compares rendered depth and colour with the observed image after ego-motion compensation. Pre-training runs for 30 epochs with a ResNet-101 backbone at 1408x512 input. Fine-tuning then uses 20% of the annotated occupancy scenes and the usual voxel classification loss, and the learned query embeddings are carried over unchanged into an OPUS-style predictor so that we can see how far the representation travels between related decoders.
CONTROLS: The reference runs are the same decoder trained from random weights and from an image backbone alone, both under the schedule used for fine-tuning. A second comparison uses a decoder pre-trained with only a single frame, which isolates the value of temporal consistency. Each configuration is repeated with three seeds and reported with a bootstrap interval over validation scenes.
COST: 480
PREDICTION: We expect mean intersection over union to rise by roughly two points over the random start, with the largest gains on small classes such as pedestrians. The claim fails if the single-frame variant reaches the same score within the seed spread.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Anchor-agnostic query pretraining for heterogeneous sparse decoders
PROPOSAL: Pre-train a decoder whose queries are initialised from a canonical set of learned three-dimensional anchors, and optimise it with a reconstruction objective on unlabelled surround-view clips from nuScenes. The anchor set is independent of the downstream design, so the same weights can then be loaded into a decoder that starts its queries in the bird's-eye plane and into one that starts them in full three-dimensional space. We shall model the transfer by projecting canonical anchors onto each downstream layout through a small learned linear map, optimise only that map for the first epochs, then unfreeze everything. Evaluate on SparseBEV and SparseOcc with a ResNet-50 backbone, using 10% of labels.
CONTROLS: Compare the canonical-anchor start against a start that copies the downstream layout directly during pretraining, and against random initialisation. Check that the linear map does not leak labels by training it on a held-out set of unlabelled scenes. Repeat everything with three seeds and examine the learning curves for signs of instability.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: We expect the canonical-anchor model to transfer to both layouts with similar gains, whereas the layout-specific start should help only its own decoder. The claim is refuted if the gain on the second layout is within seed variation of zero.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Latent query forecasting across frames for sparse perception
PROPOSAL: Pre-train a Sparse Perception Model (SPM) by asking its queries to forecast their own features in the following frame, without any rendering step. A Bird's Eye View (BEV) encoder is not used. The current frame produces a set of queries, an ego-motion transform moves their reference points forward, and a light transformer head predicts the next-frame queries, which are compared with those produced by an exponential moving average (EMA) copy of the network under a cosine loss. Use a ResNet-50 backbone, 20 epochs, unlabeled nuScenes sequences, then fine-tune on 10% of the labelled scenes. Report mean average precision (mAP) and the nuScenes detection score (NDS) on the validation split for a Sparse4D detector.
CONTROLS: Compare with random initialisation and with an image-only backbone start under the same fine-tuning schedule. Compare against a version in which the target features come from a frozen random network, to check that forecasting rather than the architecture is responsible for the gain. Repeat over three seeds.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: We expect mAP to improve by about two points at 10% labels and NDS by a smaller amount. The approach fails if the frozen random target gives the same improvement.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Distilling frozen depth priors into sparse queries
PROPOSAL: Train a DETR3D-style detector on unlabeled KITTI-360 sequences by distilling dense relative depth from a frozen monocular depth network into its queries. Each query samples the depth map at its projected reference point and predicts the local depth distribution, and a second head predicts the depth change toward the next frame given the ego pose. Pre-training lasts 40 epochs with a ResNet-50 backbone. Fine-tune on a tenth of the labeled boxes and measure mean average precision on the official validation split. Then load the pre-trained queries and decoder into a StreamPETR model to measure how the representation transfers when the architecture is different.
CONTROLS: The reference is the same detector from random weights and from an image backbone alone. A second comparison replaces the distillation target with a shuffled depth map from another scene to check that the target content matters. Three seeds are used for each setting and the labeled fraction is varied across three values.
COST: 75
PREDICTION: We expect an improvement of three average precision points at the smallest label fraction, shrinking with more labels. The study fails if the shuffled target performs like the real one.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Pseudo-occupancy from multi-frame depth as a pretraining target
PROPOSAL: Build pseudo-occupancy volumes from unlabeled clips by fusing depth predicted for neighbouring frames after ego-motion alignment, and train SparseOcc queries to reproduce those volumes with a focal loss. The pseudo-volumes are generated once offline with a frozen depth model and then kept fixed. Pretraining uses a ResNet-101 backbone for 24 epochs on nuScenes sequences, followed by fine-tuning on 20% of the annotated Occ3D scenes. Transfer is checked by loading the query embeddings and the decoder into an OPUS-style predictor and into a Sparse4D detector with a freshly initialised head.
CONTROLS: Compare against random initialisation and against a backbone-only start with the same fine-tuning schedule. Compare against pseudo-volumes built from a single frame, to measure the value of temporal fusion. Repeat each setting with three seeds and report bootstrap intervals over scenes.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: We expect mean intersection over union to improve by about two points over the random start, with a smaller gain for the detector. The method fails if single-frame pseudo-volumes give the same improvement, or if pseudo-volume errors are copied into the queries.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Label-efficiency curves for query-based pretraining
PROPOSAL: We study how the benefit of self-supervised pretraining for sparse detectors depends on the amount of unlabeled and labeled data. We pre-train a Sparse4D model with Gaussian rendering on 10%, 50% and 100% of the unlabeled nuScenes training clips, using a ResNet-50 backbone for 24 epochs, and fine-tune each checkpoint on 1%, 5% and 25% of the labeled scenes. We then load the checkpoints into SparseBEV and measure whether the curves keep their shape. We fit a simple power law to mean average precision against the number of labeled scenes for every pretraining amount.
CONTROLS: Each cell of the grid is compared with random initialisation and with a backbone-only start. We repeat every cell with three seeds and test whether the gap between pretrained and random models narrows with more labels. A final check re-runs the largest cell with a different random order of clips.
COST: 420
PREDICTION: We expect the gap to shrink with the number of labeled scenes and to grow slowly with unlabeled data. We would call the trend unreliable if the gap fluctuates by more than the seed spread across pretraining amounts.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Which parts of a sparse model transfer
PROPOSAL: Pre-train a Sparse4D detector with rendered-depth and photometric consistency on unlabeled multi-view clips from nuScenes. Then transfer subsets of the weights to a SparseBEV detector and measure each subset on its own: the image backbone, the query embeddings, the cross-attention layers of the decoder, the output heads, and every combination of the first three. Use 10% of the labeled scenes for fine-tuning and a ResNet-50 backbone throughout. Report mean average precision, nuScenes detection score and the training loss curves, and rank the parts by the improvement they bring over random initialisation.
CONTROLS: The reference runs are random initialisation and a full transfer of every part. Each subset is compared with these two anchors using identical fine-tuning schedules. Three seeds are used per subset and a paired bootstrap over validation scenes gives the intervals.
COST: 330
PREDICTION: We expect the decoder cross-attention and query embeddings to carry most of the gain, with the backbone contributing a smaller share. The conclusion fails if the ranking changes sign between seeds.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Open-vocabulary semantic rendering for occupancy queries
PROPOSAL: Pre-train SparseOcc queries by rendering per-query semantic features into the cameras and matching them to features of a frozen 2D open-vocabulary segmentation network applied to the unlabeled images. Depth consistency between adjacent frames regularises geometry. The unlabeled clips come from nuScenes, the backbone is ResNet-101, and pre-training lasts 30 epochs. Fine-tune on 20% of the Occ3D labels, then initialise the decoder of an OPUS-style predictor from the same weights. Report mean intersection over union overall and for rare classes, and the inference latency of the transferred models.
CONTROLS: Compare with random initialisation and with a backbone-only start. Compare with a variant that omits the semantic term to see how much comes from geometry alone. Repeat with three seeds. Check that the 2D network was not trained on the nuScenes validation scenes.
COST: 700
PREDICTION: Rare classes should gain the most, by roughly three points. Failure looks like a semantic term that adds no improvement beyond the depth term.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Masked image token prediction through sparse queries
PROPOSAL: Mask a large share of image patches in each camera view, let a Sparse4D decoder attend only to the visible patches through its queries, and train the queries to predict the missing patch features and the depth of the masked regions. Pre-training uses unlabeled nuScenes sequences, a ResNet-50 backbone with a feature pyramid, and 24 epochs. Fine-tune with 10% of the labeled scenes and measure mean average precision and nuScenes detection score, then transfer the decoder and queries to a StreamPETR model. Masking ratio is fixed at three quarters.
CONTROLS: Compare against random initialisation and an image-only backbone start under identical schedules. Compare against a masked autoencoder that reconstructs pixels without queries, to see whether the sparse design matters. Repeat with three seeds.
COST: 130
PREDICTION: We expect small gains of about one to two points over the backbone-only start. The idea fails if the pixel-level autoencoder transfers as well as the query-based model, which suggests that queries add little.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gaussian-rendering pretraining of Sparse4D queries on unlabeled clips
PROPOSAL: Pre-train a Sparse4D detector on unlabeled six-camera clips from nuScenes by letting each instance query emit a few 3D Gaussians, splat them into the current and adjacent frames, and supervise only with photometric and rendered-depth consistency under relative ego poses. Run 24 epochs with a ResNet-50 backbone at 704x256 resolution, then fine-tune on 10% of the labeled training scenes with the standard detection loss, and reuse the same query-to-Gaussian head to initialise a SparseOcc decoder evaluated on Occ3D. Report mean average precision, nuScenes detection score and mean intersection over union on the validation split.
CONTROLS: Compare against the same detector from random weights and against one initialised from an ImageNet backbone only, with the fine-tuning schedule held fixed. Compare against dense rendering pretraining of the same backbone, transferred through the image encoder alone. Repeat the label fraction at 5%, 10% and a quarter with three seeds each. Compare the query-to-Gaussian head frozen against the same head fine-tuned, on both the detector and the occupancy decoder.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: We expect two to three points of mean average precision over random weights when a tenth of the labels is used, with the gain shrinking as more labels arrive. The plan fails if the ImageNet-only start reaches the same score within seed variation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Rendered depth and pose consistency for pretraining sparse occupancy queries
PROPOSAL: Pre-train a SparseOcc decoder on unlabeled surround-view clips drawn from the Occ3D scenes by letting every voxel-free query predict a semantic Gaussian, rasterise the Gaussians into neighbouring cameras, and score them by reprojection error against depths implied by relative ego poses. Train 30 epochs with a ResNet-101 backbone at 1408x512 resolution, then fine-tune on 20% of the annotated occupancy scenes with the usual voxel loss, and carry the query embeddings into a StreamPETR detector evaluated on the validation split. Report mean intersection over union, mean average precision and nuScenes detection score.
CONTROLS: Compare against a dense BEV detector from random weights and against one initialised from a language-model embedding only, with the evaluation schedule held fixed. Compare against dense rendering pretraining of a different backbone, transferred through the depth head alone. Repeat the camera count across 4, 6 and 8 with three seeds each. Compare the Gaussian count per query lowered against the same count raised, on both the occupancy decoder and the detector.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: We expect two to three points of mean intersection over union over the random start when a fifth of the labels is used, with the gain shrinking as more labels arrive. The plan fails if the language-embedding start reaches the same score within seed variation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Temporal query contrastive pretraining transferred to SparseBEV
PROPOSAL: Pre-train StreamPETR on unlabeled nuScenes sequences by following each query through ego-motion compensated reference points across four consecutive frames, and pull together the features of the same 3D location with an InfoNCE loss, taking other locations from the same clip as negatives. Pre-training uses an AdamW optimiser with warm-up and random-crop augmentation for 20 epochs on a V2-99 backbone. Fine-tuning uses 5% of the labeled scenes. Transfer is measured by loading query embeddings, temporal attention layers and decoder into SparseBEV and reporting mean average precision and nuScenes detection score after 12 epochs.
CONTROLS: Compare SparseBEV fine-tuned from random weights against the same model started from a backbone-only initialisation, with data and schedule held fixed. Compare loading query embeddings alone, decoder alone and both together, to see which parts carry over. Compare negatives drawn from other locations against negatives drawn from other scenes, with seeds repeated. Compare the label fraction varied over three levels.
COST: 96
PREDICTION: Contrastive pretraining should lift mean average precision by one to three points at 5% labels, with query embeddings and decoder together giving the largest share. The study fails when the backbone-only start closes the gap within seed variation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Reprojection-error pretraining of SparseBEV with tuned optimisation
PROPOSAL: Pre-train a SparseBEV detector on unlabeled nuScenes sequences by projecting each query reference point into the adjacent frame and minimising the photometric difference at that location, using ego poses for the geometry. Training runs 16 epochs on a ResNet-101 backbone with an AdamW optimiser, warm-up and random-crop augmentation, followed by fine-tuning on 10% of the labeled scenes for 12 epochs. Mean average precision and nuScenes detection score are given on the validation split together with the final training traces.
CONTROLS: Compare an AdamW optimiser against an SGD optimiser during pretraining, with data and initialisation held fixed. Compare warm-up lengths short, medium and long on the pretraining run, with seeds repeated. Compare random-crop augmentation against colour-jitter augmentation at fine-tuning, with schedule fixed. Compare the input image width varied over 704, 1408 and 1760 pixels.
COST: 96
PREDICTION: Reprojection pretraining should lift mean average precision by one to three points at 10% labels, with the AdamW and warm-up combination giving the steadiest curves. The study fails when the optimiser change closes the gap within seed variation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Query pretraining for label-scarce sparse occupancy prediction
PROPOSAL: Pre-train a SparseOcc predictor on unlabeled nuScenes clips by predicting, for each query, a semantic Gaussian whose rendered depth must agree with pseudo-depth fused from neighbouring frames. Pre-training takes 30 epochs with a ResNet-101 backbone. Fine-tune on the Occ3D training scenes with label fractions of 2%, 5% and 10%, and evaluate mean intersection over union on the validation split, separately for rare and common classes. A transfer run loads the query embeddings into an OPUS-style predictor with a new output head.
CONTROLS: Compare the pretrained predictor against random weights at each label fraction, with the schedule held fixed. Compare the transfer to the OPUS-style predictor against its own random start, with seeds repeated. Compare rare classes against common classes, matched by number of validation voxels. Compare the pretraining data amount varied over a half and the whole training set.
COST: 640
PREDICTION: At the smallest label fractions the gain should be largest, around three points of mean intersection over union, and fade as labels accumulate. The claim fails when random weights catch up at 2% labels within seed variation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Fully supervised regime for pretrained sparse occupancy queries
PROPOSAL: Start from a SparseOcc predictor whose queries were trained on unlabeled nuScenes clips to emit a semantic Gaussian each, scored by rendered depth against pseudo-depth fused over adjacent frames. The pre-training pass takes 24 epochs on a ResNet-50 backbone. Fine-tuning then uses every annotated Occ3D training scene under the standard 24-epoch schedule, and mean intersection over union is computed on the 150 validation scenes for every semantic class. A transfer run loads the query embeddings into an OPUS-style predictor with a new output head.
CONTROLS: Compare the pretrained predictor against random weights with the complete label set, with the schedule held fixed. Compare the transfer to the OPUS-style predictor against its own random start, with seeds repeated. Compare dynamic classes against static classes, matched by number of validation voxels. Compare the fine-tuning length varied over the standard schedule and double it.
COST: 640
PREDICTION: With the complete label set the gain should be around one point of mean intersection over union and remain visible on every class. The claim fails when random weights catch up with the full schedule within seed variation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-frame geometry pretraining judged by downstream detection accuracy
PROPOSAL: Pre-train a Sparse4D detector on unlabeled nuScenes sequences with a loss that renders each query as a Gaussian into five neighbouring frames and compares rendered and measured depth after ego alignment. A ResNet-50 backbone is used for 24 epochs. After pretraining, fine-tune on 10% of the labeled scenes and transfer the decoder to SparseBEV. The decisive outcome is the change in mean average precision and nuScenes detection score on the validation split, together with the per-class average translation error.
CONTROLS: Report mean average precision and nuScenes detection score of the pretrained and randomly started models after fine-tuning, with the schedule held fixed. Report the same two scores for SparseBEV after transfer, with seeds repeated. Report the per-class translation error, matched by class frequency. Report the rendered depth error on the unlabeled pretraining clips throughout training.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Fine-tuned detection should gain two to three average precision points and the translation error should fall slightly. The idea fails if detection scores after fine-tuning stay inside seed variation of the random start.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Image reconstruction quality as the yardstick for multi-frame query pretraining
PROPOSAL: Train a Sparse4D decoder on unlabeled nuScenes sequences using a loss in which every query becomes a Gaussian, rendered into five adjacent frames and compared with measured depth after ego alignment. A ResNet-50 backbone is used for 24 epochs. Once pretraining ends, track the rendered depth and photometric reconstruction on held-out clips, and hand the decoder over to SparseBEV. The decisive outcome is the fall in rendered depth error and the rise in structural similarity on those clips, plus the per-clip reprojection error.
CONTROLS: Report rendered depth error and structural similarity of the pretrained and randomly started models after pretraining, with the schedule held fixed. Report the same two scores for SparseBEV after transfer, with seeds repeated. Report the per-clip reprojection error, matched by clip length. Report the query activation sparsity on the unlabeled clips throughout training.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Reconstruction should improve by roughly ten percent in depth error and the reprojection error should fall slightly. The idea fails if reconstruction scores after pretraining stay inside seed variation of the random start.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Transfer of pretrained queries across unlike sparse decoders
PROPOSAL: Pre-train a SparseBEV model on unlabeled nuScenes clips with a loss that matches each query's rendered depth to the measured one in the next frame, using a ResNet-50 backbone for 20 epochs. Load its query embeddings and decoder into SparseOcc, whose queries start in 3D space, and into Sparse4D, whose queries start on the bird's-eye plane. Fine-tune each on 10% of its labels and report mean intersection over union for SparseOcc and mean average precision for Sparse4D on the validation split.
CONTROLS: Compare each downstream model started from random weights against the same model started from the pretrained queries, with the schedule held fixed. Compare transfer across unlike decoders against transfer into the architecture used for pretraining, with seeds repeated. Compare the loaded decoder frozen against fine-tuned. Compare label fractions of 5% and 10%.
COST: 180
PREDICTION: Transfer into unlike decoders should keep at least half of the in-architecture gain, around one point. The study fails if the gain over the random start vanishes within seed variation for either decoder.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Comparing two pretraining objectives for sparse queries
PROPOSAL: Pre-train two SparseBEV models on unlabeled nuScenes clips, one with a loss that matches each query's rendered depth to the measured one in the next frame and one that reconstructs patch features masked at random from the visible patches. A ResNet-101 backbone and 20 epochs are used for both. Load query embeddings and decoders into SparseOcc and Sparse4D, and fine-tune each on 10% of its labels. Report mean intersection over union for SparseOcc and mean average precision for Sparse4D on the validation split.
CONTROLS: Compare each downstream model started from depth pretraining against the same model started from patch-feature pretraining, with the schedule held fixed. Compare transfer across unlike decoders against transfer into the architecture used for pretraining, with seeds repeated. Compare the loaded decoder frozen against fine-tuned. Compare label fractions of 5% and 10%.
COST: 180
PREDICTION: The depth objective should transfer better by about one point on both decoders. The study fails if the two objectives differ by less than seed variation for either decoder.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Rendering-based pretraining of sparse detector queries on unlabeled driving video
PROPOSAL: Pre-train Sparse4D and SparseOcc on unlabeled surround-view clips from nuScenes so that learned queries carry three-dimensional scene structure. Each query predicts a small set of Gaussians with positions, scales and semantic features. These are splatted into current and neighbouring cameras, and the model is trained from photometric and rendered-depth agreement under relative ego poses. Then initialise StreamPETR, SparseBEV and OPUS-style models with the learned embeddings and decoder layers, fine-tune on 10% of the labeled scenes, and compare mean average precision, nuScenes detection score and mean intersection over union with random initialisation.
CONTROLS: Compare against random weights, an image-backbone start and dense rendering pretraining. Repeat with three seeds over label fractions of 5%, 10% and 25%.
COST: 360
PREDICTION: Fine-tuned models should gain two to three points over random weights at 10% labels. The direction fails if an image-backbone start matches the gain.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Supervised sparse detectors with refined training schedules and larger backbones
PROPOSAL: Improve Sparse4D and SparseOcc on nuScenes by strengthening supervised training with all available labels. Replace the ResNet-50 backbone with a V2-99 backbone, lengthen the schedule, add class-balanced sampling and temporal test-time augmentation, and average weights over the final checkpoints. Then retrain StreamPETR, SparseBEV and OPUS-style models using the same recipe, and compare mean average precision, nuScenes detection score and mean intersection over union with each model's standard recipe on the validation split.
CONTROLS: Compare against the standard recipe, a longer schedule and a larger backbone. Repeat with three seeds over augmentation strengths of mild, medium and strong.
COST: 360
PREDICTION: Retrained models should gain one to two points over the standard recipe on the full label set. The direction fails if the larger backbone matches the gain.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Ego-motion reprojection consistency for pretraining query decoders
PROPOSAL: Pre-train a Sparse4D decoder on unlabeled six-camera sequences by projecting every query reference point into the next frame with the ego pose, sampling image features there, and requiring them to match after feature extraction from both frames. Depth is predicted by a light head so that the projected locations follow the scene geometry. The backbone is ResNet-50 and training lasts 20 epochs. Fine-tune on 10% of labels and transfer decoder and query embeddings to SparseBEV and StreamPETR. Report mean average precision and nuScenes detection score on the validation split.
CONTROLS: Compare against random weights and a backbone-only start. Repeat with three seeds at label fractions of 5%, 10% and 25%.
COST: 72
PREDICTION: Transfer to both detectors should give one to three points at 10% labels. The direction fails if the backbone-only start gives a similar result.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Token pruning and quantisation to speed up sparse detector inference
PROPOSAL: Reduce the inference latency of a Sparse4D decoder on nuScenes by pruning image tokens that receive low attention from the queries and quantising decoder weights to eight bits. A light head predicts which tokens to keep, and the pruning ratio increases with decoder depth. The backbone is ResNet-50 and the pruned model is fine-tuned for 20 epochs. Evaluate on 10% of the training data and transfer the recipe to SparseBEV and StreamPETR. Report mean average precision, nuScenes detection score and latency on the validation split.
CONTROLS: Compare against the unpruned model and a half-precision variant. Repeat with three seeds at pruning ratios of 20%, 40% and 60%.
COST: 72
PREDICTION: The pruned models should lose under one point while cutting latency noticeably. The direction fails if accuracy falls by more than that.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Canonical anchor pretraining for heterogeneous sparse decoders
PROPOSAL: Pre-train a decoder with a canonical set of learned 3D anchors on unlabeled nuScenes clips through Gaussian rendering and depth agreement, then map those anchors to each downstream query layout through a small learned projection. One target initialises queries on the bird's-eye plane and another in full 3D space. Evaluate SparseBEV and SparseOcc with a ResNet-50 backbone after fine-tuning on 10% of the labels, and report mean average precision and mean intersection over union for the two layouts.
CONTROLS: Compare against random weights, a start copied from the layout of the target, and a backbone-only start. Repeat with three seeds at label fractions of 5% and 10%.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: The canonical start should transfer to both layouts with similar gains of about two points. The direction fails if only one layout benefits.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Teacher-student distillation for compact sparse decoders
PROPOSAL: Train a compact Sparse4D student with a ResNet-18 backbone by distilling the outputs of a large supervised teacher with a V2-99 backbone on the labeled nuScenes training scenes. The student matches teacher query features, box predictions and occupancy logits, with a projection aligning widths. Evaluate SparseBEV and SparseOcc students after the same distillation, and report mean average precision and mean intersection over union relative to the teacher on the validation split.
CONTROLS: Compare against the student trained alone, the teacher, and a student distilled on 10% of the labels. Repeat with three seeds at label fractions of 25% and 100%.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: The student should recover most of the teacher accuracy with a smaller model. The direction fails if the gap to the teacher stays large.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Label-efficiency of query pretraining as unlabeled data grows
PROPOSAL: Pre-train Sparse4D with Gaussian rendering on 10%, 50% and 100% of the unlabeled nuScenes training clips, with a ResNet-50 backbone for 24 epochs, and fine-tune each checkpoint on 1%, 5% and 25% of the labeled scenes. Load the checkpoints into SparseBEV to see whether the curves hold. Fit a saturating curve of mean average precision against labeled scenes for each amount of pretraining data, and report the labels saved at fixed accuracy.
CONTROLS: Compare against random weights and a backbone-only start in every cell. Repeat with three seeds and shuffled clip order.
COST: 420
PREDICTION: Savings in labels should grow with unlabeled data and shrink with more labels. The direction fails if the curves overlap within seed variation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Backbone scaling laws for supervised sparse detectors
PROPOSAL: Train Sparse4D with ResNet-18, ResNet-50, ResNet-101 and V2-99 backbones on 1%, 5%, 25% and 100% of the labeled nuScenes scenes, 24 epochs each, and fit a power law of mean average precision against parameter count for every label fraction. Repeat with SparseBEV to see whether the exponents agree. Report the parameter count needed to reach a given accuracy at each label fraction.
CONTROLS: Compare against the smallest backbone and a dense BEV detector in every cell. Repeat with three seeds and shuffled scene order.
COST: 420
PREDICTION: Accuracy should rise with parameter count and saturate for small label fractions. The direction fails if exponents differ between detectors.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Open-vocabulary semantic rendering for sparse occupancy queries
PROPOSAL: Pre-train SparseOcc queries by rendering per-query semantic features into the cameras and matching them to features of a frozen 2D segmentation network on unlabeled nuScenes clips, while depth agreement between adjacent frames regularises geometry. Use ResNet-101 for 30 epochs, then fine-tune on 20% of the Occ3D labels and load the decoder into an OPUS-style predictor. Report mean intersection over union overall and for rare classes on the validation split.
CONTROLS: Compare against random weights, a backbone-only start and a geometry-only variant. Repeat with three seeds at label fractions of 5% and 20%.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: Rare classes should gain about three points over random weights. The direction fails if the geometry-only variant matches the gain.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Class-balanced voxel losses for supervised sparse occupancy prediction
PROPOSAL: Train SparseOcc on the Occ3D scenes with a combination of lovasz and focal losses weighted by inverse class frequency, plus a boundary-aware term that penalises errors on voxel surfaces. Use ResNet-101 for 30 epochs and the complete label set, then apply the same loss to an OPUS-style predictor. Report mean intersection over union overall and for rare classes on the validation split.
CONTROLS: Compare against the standard loss, a focal-only variant and a frequency-weighted variant. Repeat with three seeds at loss weights of 0.5, 1 and 2.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: Rare classes should gain about two points over the standard loss. The direction fails if the focal-only variant matches the gain.
